title: E.T. Thomas and his teacher
summary: Duhé praises E.T. Thomas as a high-register trumpeter trained under Professor O'Jay in Crowley.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Who were the best trumpet players you ever heard, would you say? I've never heard no one, no better than E.T. Thomas.
Really? For high, high workout. For high register. He was, he was, well, how strong, you know what he is.

High C's. Somebody said he was trained up in Boston or so. No, sir, he was trained under Professor O'Jay right in Crowley. Oh, right in Crowley. Yeah, the man there, Professor O'Jay, had five years conservatory playing in all foreign countries. He played from a bazoon up. And you'd whistle a tune and you'd have a white shirt and you'd write the lead sheet, and about an hour he'd have an arrangement for a six-piece band, and how great he was.
